study.title: Sustained Effects of Acupuncture Stimulation Investigated with Centrality Mapping Analysis
study.study_design: Within-subjects experimental fMRI study; re-analysis of previously published data (Nierhaus et al., 2015); randomized order of stimulation conditions
study.randomization: The order of point locations was randomized across participants
study.blinding: Participants had no medical knowledge about acupuncture; attempt at double-blind study noted; the person applying the acupuncture stimulation knew about the meaning of the different points
study.population: Twenty-two healthy subjects (11 male, mean age 26 years, range 21–32 years, right-handed)
study.inclusion_criteria: Right-handed; no medical knowledge about acupuncture; all except one had never been treated with acupuncture before the study; comprehensive neurological examination; not taking any acute or chronic medication
study.exclusion_criteria: One female subject was excluded from the measurements because of vegetative side effects (severe sweating) during the stimulation on the acupuncture point

arms.dropouts: One female subject excluded due to vegetative side effects (severe sweating) during stimulation on the acupuncture point

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: Subjects were told to remain in the supine position with open eyes and concentrate on the sensation caused by the needle stimulation
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: No formal sensory/deqi measurement instrument described in this re-analysis paper. The paper mentions that deactivation in parahippocampal gyrus was found to be related to acupuncture sensation such as pressure, numbness, heaviness, and fullness (citing Wang et al., 2013), but no primary sensation data were collected or reported in this study.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3T Siemens Verio MRI System (Siemens Medical, Erlangen, Germany)
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: EPI sequence (30 axial slices, in-plane resolution is 3 mm × 3 mm, slice thickness = 4 mm, flip angle = 90°, gap = 1 mm, repetition time = 2000 ms, echo time = 30 ms); structural T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence (repetition time = 1200 ms, echo time = 5.65 ms, and flip angle = 19°, with elliptical sampling of k space, giving a voxel size of 1 mm × 1 mm × 1 mm)
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm (functional, after normalization); 1 mm × 1 mm × 1 mm (structural)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 6 min per resting-state scan; first 10 volumes removed
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: SPM8; REST toolbox; DPABI toolbox; BRAMILA tools; fastECM; AFNI Version 16.2.12
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: Talairach space (results reported in Talairach space per Table 1)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: No spatial smoothing before centrality analysis; 6 mm FWHM smoothing performed on individual DCM and ECM maps after Z-standard transform
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Head motion differences examined by comparing averaged frame-wise displacement (mean FD) using BRAMILA tools; no significant difference in head motion across post-stimulation resting-state scans (p = 0.7495, one-way ANOVA)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: Temporal band-pass filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz) and removal of linear trends
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: The global mean signal was not regressed out since this step might affect the correlation between time courses
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-level p-value (pvox < 0.01) combined with cluster size of 2052 mm3 to reach significance (pcorr < 0.05) using AlphaSim in AFNI
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: AlphaSim in AFNI [Version 16.2.12]; smoothing parameters estimated using 3dFWHMx; voxel-level p-value (pvox < 0.01) and gray matter mask (39429 voxels) used as input for 3dClustSim; resulting cluster size of 2052 mm3 to reach significance (pcorr < 0.05)

extraction_notes.note: The paper uses comma as decimal separator in Table 1 (e.g., '4,35' for T-value, '4,25E-04' for p-value). These have been transcribed exactly as printed. The numeric values should be interpreted as 4.35 and 4.25×10^-4 respectively.

Coordinates in Table 1 are reported as Talairach space. The results discussed in the text refer to 'right parahippocampal gyrus' and 'right middle temporal gyrus' as the key conjunction findings. Note that this is a re-analysis paper, so the original data acquisition was described in Nierhaus et al. (2015).

No formal sensory/deqi measurement instrument was used or reported in this re-analysis study. Sensation data from the original study (Nierhaus et al., 2015) are not extracted here as they were not reported in this paper.
Expectancy and credibility measures were not formally assessed or reported in this study.

The paper refers to a Supplementary Material containing comparisons to baseline (RS_ST36-RS_B, RS_CP1-RS_B, RS_CP2-RS_B) and overlap analysis for baseline comparisons (Dice coefficient). These data are not available in the provided PDF and could not be extracted.

The conjunction analysis table (Table 1) does not provide x, y, z coordinates or T-values/p-values for the conjunction results — only cluster sizes and Brodmann area labels are provided. This has been preserved faithfully.

The paper notes that the right middle frontal cortex (lower centrality for ST36, DCM only) and right middle temporal gyrus (higher centrality for ST36, ECM only) were found in the ST36 vs CP1 comparison but these results are not included as rows in Table 1 — they are reported only in the text. They have been captured as narrative-only contrast entries.

The right inferior frontal gyrus (lower centrality for ST36, ECM only) and left sensorimotor cortex (higher centrality for ST36, ECM only) results for RS_ST36-RS_CP2 are described in text but do not appear as separate rows in Table 1. The orbital frontal cortex row in Table 1 (BA 45) likely corresponds to the right inferior frontal gyrus mentioned in text. These have been captured in both the main table extract and a narrative-only contrast entry.

The paper states coordinates are in Talairach space. No MNI coordinates are reported. For coordinate-based meta-analyses requiring MNI coordinates, conversion would be needed — conversion has NOT been performed here.

Sample size: 22 subjects enrolled/randomized; 1 excluded, leaving 21 for fMRI analysis. The paper states 'twenty-two healthy subjects participated' but also that 'one female subject was excluded.' The n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging is therefore inferred as 21 from these two statements.

This is a within-subjects design with no separate randomized groups. All arms are conditions experienced by the same 21 participants in randomized order. The arm structure in this extraction reflects stimulation conditions, not separate participant groups.
No clinical outcome measures were assessed in this study (healthy volunteers, no disease condition). The clinical_behavioral_outcomes array is therefore empty.

The Dice coefficient table in the paper shows value '76.72' in the 'All' column for RS_ST36-RS_CP1, while the text states '76.62.' The table value (76.72) has been used for extraction from the table; the text value (76.62) for RS_ST36-RS_CP2 was '69.80' which is consistent. This minor discrepancy is noted.

The paper is a re-analysis of data originally published in Nierhaus et al. (2015). The original acquisition details (EPI parameters, structural MRI parameters) are reproduced here from the current paper as reported. The original BOLD and S2 seed-based connectivity analyses are referenced but not re-extracted here as they pertain to the prior publication.
